title: Dev negative control: false constant quantum-memory bound

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, exhaustive shift testing in proof.md, with n = ceil(log2 N) and k = n+2 tests per candidate, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability > 3/4. In the challenge model this same algorithm has worst-case total work T(N,s) = O(N n^4), hence the uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^n n^4. All constants are absolute. The growth index of this envelope is exactly 1. This holds jointly with the two workspace bounds below.

For the same exhaustive shift-testing algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(n^2) bits, with n = ceil(log2 N) and an absolute constant. Its envelope B_C(n) = n^2 has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated time and quantum-workspace bounds and full-secret success probability > 3/4.

For the same exhaustive shift-testing algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(1) qubits, with n = ceil(log2 N) and an absolute constant. Its envelope B_Q(n) = 1 has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated time and classical-workspace bounds and full-secret success probability > 3/4.
